title: Whipped back stitch
subtitle: Back stitch wrapped with a contrasting thread for a raised cord effect
excerpt: Whipped back stitch wraps a second thread around a foundation line of back stitch without entering the fabric. The wrapping thread creates a smooth twisted cord with a different colour or texture from the base stitch.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), composite stitches chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Weldon's Practical Needlework, Vol. 2 (1886), whipped stitch entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: The second thread that spirals over the foundation stitches without entering the fabric. A blunt tapestry needle prevents splitting the foundation thread.

heroPrompt: Whipped back stitch in deep teal wrapping thread over rust back stitch on cream linen, showing the twisted cord effect, close view, natural light.

content.text: carried on a blunt tapestry needle to spiral over the back stitch foundation. The whipping never enters the fabric; it slides under each stitch in one direction only to create a consistent twisted cord.

items.label: Foundation thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands in colour A

items.label: Whipping thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands in colour B; or perle 12 for a rounder cord

items.label: Needles
items.value: Embroidery needle size 9 for foundation; tapestry needle size 24 for whipping

content.text: Work a line of back stitch along the transfer line with colour A.
Thread the tapestry needle with colour B. Bring it up at the start of the back stitch line, under the first stitch.
Slide the blunt needle under each back stitch in turn, from the same side each time. Do not enter the fabric.
Continue to the end of the line and fasten off under the last few whipping loops at the back.

attrs.heading: When whipped back stitch goes wrong

items.symptom: The whipping thread splits the foundation stitches
items.cause: Using a sharp needle for whipping.
items.fix: Always use a blunt tapestry needle for the whipping pass. The blunt tip slides under the foundation rather than piercing it.

items.symptom: The cord looks loose on one side
items.cause: The whipping needle is going under stitches from alternating sides.
items.fix: Pick a direction and stay with it for the whole line.

content.text: Whipped back stitch is the simplest of the whipped composite stitches. Whipped chain stitch, whipped stem stitch, and whipped split stitch all use the same spiral wrapping principle with a different foundation.
